title: Epochal window misalignment causing thin batches and tail spikes
creator: Sofia Ruiz
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-17 we observed recurring short bursts of elevated P95/P99 latency for the hosted inference surface. The primary user-visible symptom was a sudden increase in response tail latency for small, low-token requests. These spikes corresponded with a drop in average batch utilization and a large increase in the fraction of batches that contained only a single request (batch thinness).

Scope: Affected both hosted API instances in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 intermittently over a 12-hour window. Estimated ~3% of requests in the window saw >2x latency; major customers reported transient QoS degradation but no data loss.

Investigation summary: We traced the root cause to a misalignment between two adaptive components: the ingress sequencer's per-shard emission phase (a probabilistic jitter introduced in 2025-Q4 to reduce correlated bursts) and the continuous batcher's adaptive window estimator. Under certain traffic mixes (high small-request ratio with variable arrival jitter), the sequencer jitter caused request emission to cluster into micro-phases that fell just outside the batcher's alignment threshold. The batcher then frequently closed windows prematurely, producing many 1-request batches. These thin batches bypassed efficient GPU execution paths, increasing per-request overhead and causing tail latency amplification.

Root cause: Regression introduced by PR #GH-8402 (sequencer jitter fine-tuning) combined with a previously unnoticed sensitivity in the adaptive-window estimator when mean inter-arrival variance exceeded the configured threshold. The two controls were independently safe but interacted poorly for certain traffic spectrums.

Why previous safeguards didn't catch it: Canary and staging workloads lacked the same small-request-heavy distribution and the sequencer jitter config was not mirrored in dedicated test harnesses. Unit tests exercised window bounds but not the joint interaction across the sequencer and batcher.
timeline: 2026-02-17 03:22 UTC - First alert: P99 latency > target in us-west-2. Automated detector flagged increased single-request batch ratio.
2026-02-17 04:10 UTC - On-call engineer (Liam) triaged; identified spike correlating with batch thinness via live dashboard (links below).
2026-02-17 05:30 UTC - Rollback of sequencer jitter delta on a subset of instances reduced spikes; mitigated customer impact.
2026-02-17 09:00 UTC - Full mitigation rollout completed. Post-rollout monitoring showed latency returning to baseline over 30m window.
2026-02-18 10:00 UTC - Deep dive initiated. Formed cross-team task force with runtime, serving, and QA reps.
analysis: Batching telemetry: single-request batch fraction rose from baseline 6% to 48% during the incident windows; average batch size dropped from 3.8 to 1.1.
CPU/GPU profiling: increased kernel launch overhead dominated; GPU utilization fell by ~22% on affected nodes despite increased request rate.

Config delta: GH-8402 changed sequencer emission jitter from +/-2ms to +/-8ms for high-throughput shards to smooth long-tail bursts. This widened phase dispersion and interacted with the batcher alignment window of 10ms.
Repro: Synthetic harness replicating small-request-heavy traffic with sequencer jitter >=6ms reproduces thin-batch formation and P99 amplification locally.

Repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/tree/main/batcher-repro - traffic generator used for reproduction
action_items: ENG-118777: Add a joint integration test that runs the sequencer with production-like jitter against the continuous batcher harness (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-03)
ENG-118778: Harden adaptive-window estimator to be robust to phase dispersion by introducing a phase-aware sliding window and hysteresis (owner: Liam O'Connor, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-17)
Backport: Apply a conservative sequencer jitter cap in runtime-1.20 stable branch until integration tests land (owner: runtime oncall, estimate: 1, due: 2026-02-20)
Observability: Add a derived metric 'batch_phase_skew' and alert when single-request batch fraction > 20% for >5 minutes (owner: Platform Observability, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-05)

Load testing: Expand smoke/staging workloads to include small-request-heavy scenarios and run nightly batcher stress tests with varied jitter settings (owner: QA Automation, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-10)
Customer comms: Reach out to the 4 customers who reported impacts with a summary and mitigation steps (owner: Customer Success, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-01)
Retro & docs: Document the interaction class in the reliability playbook and add a troubleshooting checklist (owner: Reliability Engineering, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-12)
updates: 2026-02-20 - Priya Nair: Initial integration test PR created (GH-8479). Test covers jitter values 0-12ms and asserts batch size distribution remains within 15% of baseline.
2026-02-24 - QA Automation: Nightly harness extended; first run shows failure at jitter=8ms; attached logs to GH-8479.
2026-03-01 - Customer Success: Outreach sent to affected customers; two requested deeper logs which are provided via secure share.
2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: Proposed adaptive-window change landed as draft RFC; reviewers requested microbenchmark results before merging.
2026-03-09 - Observability: batch_phase_skew metric added to staging and alerting threshold tuned; no false positives seen in 72h burn-in.
2026-03-10 - Lead review (Amina Patel): Recommend merging the phased-window heuristic and stabilizing sequencer jitter cap in next runtime patch. Moving ticket to In Review.
review_feedback: Amina Patel (Lead, Runtime): Please include cost/perf tradeoffs in the RFC for phased-window; ensure we don't regress throughput for long-request streams.
Dmitri Volkov (QA): Need deterministic unit tests for the edge cases where arrival variance toggles the hysteresis boundary.
Priya Nair (Infra): Consider a feature flag to ramp phased-window changes per cluster to reduce blast radius.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation: scaled back sequencer jitter to +/-3ms and rolled back the 8ms tuning across hosted clusters on 2026-02-17; this returned batch size and latency metrics to baseline. Long-term: phased-window estimator and integration tests in flight; observability improvements landed to detect similar regressions earlier.
postmortem_status: Action items created and assigned; technical RFC under review; monitoring alerts in place; ready for final review and retro session.
